q: What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, Mg = 24)
A hydrocarbon contains 2.4 g of carbon and 0.6 g of hydrogen. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12)
explain: Moles: C = 2.4 ÷ 12 = 0.20; H = 0.6 ÷ 1 = 0.6. The ratio is 1 : 3, so the empirical formula is CH₃.

q: Iron(III) ions are Fe³⁺ and sulfate ions are SO₄²⁻. What is the formula of iron(III) sulfate?
explain: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6: two Fe³⁺ (+6) balance three SO₄²⁻ (−6).

q: What is the amount, in moles, of 11 g of carbon dioxide, CO₂? (Ar: C = 12, O = 16)
explain: Mr of CO₂ = 44. Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 11 ÷ 44 = 0.25 mol.

q: A model of a molecule shows one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms. What is the formula of the compound?
explain: The model has 1 carbon atom and 4 hydrogen atoms, so the formula is CH₄ (methane).

q: Chlorine has two isotopes: 75% is chlorine-35 and 25% is chlorine-37. What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine?
What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃? (Ar: O = 16, Fe = 56)
Which pair of units can be used for the concentration of a solution?
explain: Concentration is the amount of solute (in g or mol) in 1 dm³ of solution, so g/dm³ and mol/dm³.

q: Which sample contains the same number of atoms as 12 g of carbon? (Ar: C = 12, Mg = 24)
explain: 12 g of carbon is 1 mol of atoms. 24 g of magnesium is also 1 mol (24 ÷ 24), so it has the same number of atoms.

q: Which statement describes the molecular formula of a compound?
options: The number and type of different atoms in one molecule of the compound
The simplest whole number ratio of the atoms in the compound
The total number of atoms in one mole of the compound
The number of molecules in one gram of the compound
explain: A molecular formula shows the actual number of each type of atom in one molecule, for example C₂H₆ for ethane. The simplest ratio is the empirical formula.

q: Which row gives the correct name and formula?
explain: Ammonia is NH₃. Carbon dioxide is CO₂ (CO is carbon monoxide), water is H₂O and methane is CH₄.

q: Which gas has the largest relative molecular mass? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)
explain: Mr values: SO₂ = 64, N₂ = 28, CO = 28 and NH₃ = 17, so SO₂ is the largest.

q: What is the relative molecular mass, Mr, of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, S = 32)
A sample of 0.20 mol of a metal M has a mass of 13 g. What is the relative atomic mass of M?
explain: Molar mass = mass ÷ moles = 13 ÷ 0.20 = 65 g/mol, so Ar = 65.

q: Aqueous calcium hydroxide neutralises aqueous nitric acid, forming aqueous calcium nitrate and water. Which is the correct balanced equation?
explain: Two OH⁻ ions need two H⁺ ions, and calcium nitrate is Ca(NO₃)₂, giving 2H₂O in total.

q: Copper(II) carbonate is heated and decomposes. Which word equation is correct?
options: copper(II) carbonate → copper(II) oxide + carbon dioxide
copper(II) carbonate → copper + carbon dioxide + oxygen
copper(II) carbonate → copper(II) oxide + carbon monoxide
explain: Metal carbonates such as copper(II) carbonate decompose on heating to the metal oxide and carbon dioxide.

q: A model of an ionic lattice shows alternating calcium ions (Ca²⁺) and fluoride ions (F⁻), with twice as many fluoride ions as calcium ions. What is the formula of the compound?
explain: The ions are in the ratio 1 Ca²⁺ : 2 F⁻, which balances the charge, giving CaF₂.

q: Fe₂O₃(s) + ?CO(g) → ?Fe(l) + ?CO₂(g). What are the numbers in front of CO, Fe and CO₂ in the balanced equation?
explain: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ has 2 Fe, 3 C and 6 O on each side.

q: Which word equation shows sodium hydroxide being neutralised by hydrochloric acid?
options: sodium hydroxide + hydrochloric acid → sodium chloride + hydrogen
sodium hydroxide + hydrochloric acid → sodium oxide + water
sodium hydroxide + hydrochloric acid → sodium + chlorine + water
sodium hydroxide + hydrochloric acid → sodium chloride + water
explain: An alkali and an acid react to form a salt and water. The salt from hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide is sodium chloride.

q: What is the percentage by mass of water in hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄·5H₂O? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 64)
explain: Mr = 160 + 90 = 250. Percentage of water = 90 ÷ 250 × 100 = 36%.

q: Four solutions of the same solute are made. Which is the most concentrated?
explain: In g/dm³ the concentrations are 10, 8, 5 and 6 respectively, so 1 g in 100 cm³ (10 g/dm³) is the highest.

q: What does a concentration of 0.5 mol/dm³ mean?
options: There is 0.5 mol of solute in every 1 dm³ of solution
There is 0.5 g of solute in every 1 dm³ of solution
There is 0.5 mol of solute in every 1 cm³ of solution
There is 0.5 mol of solute in 100 cm³ of water
explain: mol/dm³ means moles of solute per dm³ of the whole solution.

q: A clean iron nail is placed in blue copper(II) sulfate solution. Solid copper forms and a pale green solution of iron(II) sulfate remains. Which equation has the correct state symbols?
explain: The iron nail and the copper formed are solids (s), while both salts are dissolved in water, (aq).

q: What is the percentage by mass of magnesium in magnesium oxide, MgO? (Ar: O = 16, Mg = 24)
explain: Mr of MgO = 40. Percentage of Mg = 24 ÷ 40 × 100 = 60%.

q: What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄? (Ar: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)
Which row correctly gives the ions present and the formula of the compound?
explain: Ca²⁺ needs two Cl⁻ to balance charge. The correct formulae of the others are Na₂O, AlCl₃ and K₂SO₄.

q: What is 0.025 dm³ in cm³?
4.0 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in water and made up to 500 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration in mol/dm³? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
explain: Moles = 4.0 ÷ 40 = 0.10 mol. Concentration = 0.10 ÷ 0.500 dm³ = 0.20 mol/dm³.

q: 2.50 g of impure limestone reacts with excess hydrochloric acid and gives 0.0150 mol of carbon dioxide. Assume the impurities do not react. What is the percentage purity of the calcium carbonate? (Ar: C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40)
Glucose has the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆. What is its empirical formula?
explain: Divide the numbers of atoms by their highest common factor, 6, to give C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1.
